Apple last week launched what can be considered its first batch of AI wearables, including the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Both products, beyond introducing Siri AI, also feature a new 'Audio Intelligence' function. However, according to a Bloomberg report today, another AI product — the rumoured wearable pendant — has been temporarily shelved.

Apple's AI wearable plans, at least for now, no longer include a pendant

The AI era has driven plenty of software innovation, but it has yet to truly translate into an entirely new category of products.

Of course, there have been attempts, such as the failed Humane Ai Pin. Meta's AI smart glasses have also achieved some success, but this market remains relatively niche.

Rumours suggest Apple has multiple AI-centric wearables in development. The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 launched by Apple last week can be considered among the first products to hit the market.

However, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple has been developing a wearable pendant equipped with a camera. But it sounds like progress on this product has currently stalled.

Gurman previously reported that this pendant would 'serve as an always-on camera for the iPhone, while featuring a built-in microphone for Siri input'.

It now appears Apple has decided to pause this project. The company's current focus is integrating AI into the Apple Watch, while also developing new AirPods equipped with a camera, as well as smart glasses expected to launch in 2027.

It remains unclear how AI will be integrated into these devices, but Gurman also mentioned that Apple is exploring a new screenless, health-focused wearable, hoping to compete more effectively with WHOOP.

Would you be interested in an AI pendant product designed by Apple? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
